L288: ### アイテムキャッチ
L289: 
L290: ファイターのアイテム取得範囲と、アイテムの拾われ判定が重なっているとき、ファイターはアイテムを取得することができる。
L291: このとき、アイテムの種類が「キャッチ（保持）可能」であれば、cite153†ファイター はアイテムをキャッチする。
L292: なお、2人以上のファイターがまったく同時にアイテムを取得しようと試みた場合、必ずプレイヤー番号の最も小さいファイターがアイテムを取得する。
L293: 
L294: アイテムを取得する方法には、以下のものがある。
L295:   1. 地上
L296:      * 地上アイテム拾い
L297:        * その場アイテム拾い
L298:        * 前傾（歩き）アイテム拾い
L299:      * ダッシュ攻撃拾い
L300:      * 強攻撃拾い
L301:   2. 空中
L302:      * 空中その場取得
L303:      * 空中攻撃の出始め
L304:      * 空中回避の出始め
L305:   3. 特殊
L306:      * cite169†Image†img.atwiki.jp cite170†Image†img.atwiki.jp のつかみ
L307:      * cite169†Image†img.atwiki.jp cite170†Image†img.atwiki.jp の通常必殺ワザ
L308:      * cite171†Image†img.atwiki.jp の下必殺ワザ
L309:      * cite172†Image†img.atwiki.jp の上必殺ワザ（通常時）
L310:      * スピリットの「オートキャッチャー」
L311: 
L312: * * *
L313: ### キャッチの種類と受付時間
L314: 
L315: キャッチの種類によって、アイテム取得の受付時間が異なる。
L316: 
L317: 取得種類  | 受付時間
L318: --- | ---
L319: その場アイテム拾い
L320: （地上・空中）  | 1F目のみ
L321: ダッシュ攻撃  | 1-5F
L322: 強攻撃  | 1-2F
L323: 空中攻撃  | 1-4F
L324: 空中回避  | 1-5F
L325: 
L326: * * *
L327: ### アイテム取得範囲
L328: 
L329: ファイターのアイテム取得範囲は長方形である。
L330: 長方形の大きさは、ファイターごとに次のパラメータで決まっている。
L331: 
L332:   * 地上版
L333:     * item_range_front
L334:     * item_range_front_max
L335:     * item_range_back
L336:     * item_range_h
L337:   * 空中版
L338:     * item_range_air_front
L339:     * item_range_air_back
L340:     * item_range_air_h
L341: 
L342: 地上版は前方向に広く、空中版は上下方向に広い。
L343: 振り向いて強攻撃を出した場合も、もともとの向きでfront/backが処理される。
L344: 地上版のitem_range_front_maxは、横強攻撃で取得するときにのみ（？）使われる。
L345: 
L346: cite173†Image†img.atwiki.jp cite174†Image†img.atwiki.jp L347: 
L348: ↑ 地上取得範囲（上）、空中取得範囲（下）。画像はforの解析ツールで作成。
L349: アイテムの拾われ判定は長方形。
L350: なお、拾われ判定・アイテムの食らい判定・cite66†攻撃判定 はすべて別物である。
L351:

L17: Donkey Kong (ドンキーコング, Donkey Kong) is a playable character in cite2†Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . Initially teased in the then-unnamed Ultimate's announcement trailer, Donkey Kong was, like all veterans, confirmed on June 12th, 2018. He is classified as cite13†Fighter #02 .
L18: 
L19: Donkey Kong retains his gorilla-like grunts and roars from cite14†Super Smash Bros. 4 , rather than using his voice actor, cite15†Takashi Nagasako†en.wikipedia.org .
L20: Donkey Kong is ranked 46th out of 82 on the current tier list, placing him at the end of the B+ tier. This is a moderate drop from his 22nd out of 54 placement in SSB4. Donkey Kong has surprisingly good mobility for a super-heavyweight, having above-average speed both on and off the ground, without giving up much KO power in return.
L21: He has a plethora of cite16†meteor smashes (his forward and down aerials, cite17†Headbutt , and cite18†Hand Slap ), which gives him many options to net reverse-edgeguards and early kills on recovering opponents. His aerials all serve a purpose in his strong advantage state, with his back aerial often being considered one of the best in the game.
L22: Donkey Kong also possesses one of the most versatile throws in the game with his cargo throw, which can set up edgeguards, net early kill confirms on platforms, and KO outright if opponents DI incorrectly. His specials are also effective for hard punishes and unconventional edgeguarding, making for a respectable moveset overall.
L23: To contrast a slew of desirable moves and attributes, Donkey Kong is held back by notable flaws, the biggest being his disadvantage state, which is among the worst in the game. He has one of the largest hurtboxes, even bigger than his model would suggest, and many of his moves stick his large arms out, often causing him to get clipped by attacks even when attacking or rolling/spotdodging.
L24: He also has little to no options to escape from combos or relieve pressure due to a frame 4 air dodge, and lack of moves that are fast enough to break combos, while most of his out-of-shield options are too slow or risky to be practical. His recovery is also one of the most exploitable in the game, as a simple spike is enough for Donkey Kong to quickly lose his stock, since cite19†Spinning Kong is easily intercepted from above, and offers very little vertical distance.
L25: Alongside this, Donkey Kong has a lackluster and risky cite20†neutral game , as many of his attacks have high ending lag and a decent chunk of them are unsafe on hit at low percents.
L26: Overall, Donkey Kong is a speedy heavyweight with unique tools and the potential to convert a single throw or edgeguard into early KOs; however, his disadvantage state means a simple mistake can make it hard for him to fight at all.
L27: Although initially unpopular in competitive play, Donkey Kong's representation and results gradually improved in the post-cite21†pandemic metagame thanks to the efforts of players such as cite22†ChunkyKong and cite23†HIKARU , before exploding in 2024 thanks to the efforts of other players such as cite24†Mild na H.O and cite25†Rarikkusu .
L28: ## Attributes[cite26†edit ]
L29: Donkey Kong is unsurprisingly a large super-heavycite27†weight , having the same weight value as cite28†King Dedede , and is the third-heaviest character in the game behind cite29†Bowser and cite30†King K. Rool . Despite this, he is one of the fastest heavy characters in the game, both in terms of general mobility and attack speed.
L30: He has the 10th fastest cite31†walking speed, the 29th fastest cite32†dashing speed, the 16th highest cite33†traction , above average cite34†falling speed and jumping force, and is tied with cite35†Mario , cite36†Sonic , cite37†Little Mac , and cite38†Inkling for the 13th fastest cite39†air speed . In contrast, he has below average cite40†gravity and moderately slow cite41†air acceleration .
L31: A typical heavyweight is expected to possess moves with high power, and Donkey Kong is no exception to this — it is possibly his greatest attribute. Donkey Kong has no problem with setting up into KOs with moves that have both high power and decent cite42†range : his sweetspotted up tilt, smash attacks, aerials, back throw, cite43†Giant Punch , and grounded cite19†Spinning Kong are all prime examples. His ability to take stocks with his powerful attacks is made easier with his decent approach.
L32: His mobility and size work together to give him an effective grounded approach and longer range, respectively. All of these attributes combined allow him to have an easier time fighting in close quarters and landing attacks on his opponents. He also has very strong survivability thanks to his aforementioned high weight and above-average falling speed, which is also common for his archetype.
L33: In total, Donkey Kong's attributes give him some of the best overall endurance in the game, with only cite29†Bowser and cite30†King K. Rool surpassing him horizontally.
L34: Donkey Kong works well with his grounded moveset. His neutral attack has decent damage and startup. His forward tilt's long range makes it one of his main spacing tools and works better with its intangibility. His up tilt is a safe move to interrupt his opponents, with the move covering Donkey Kong's entire body, acting as an anti-air, and hitting through low platforms such as the ones on cite44†Battlefield . His down tilt gives him a long-range crouching option and has a chance to cite45†trip opponents.
L35: His dash attack works as a combo starter and a situational KO option at low and very high percentages, respectively. All of his smash attacks are notoriously strong and relatively fast, making them his go-to options for hard reads and scoring KOs. His aerial options also have considerable utility. His forward and down aerials are some of his best edgeguarding tools due to both of them being cite16†meteor smashes .
L36: His neutral aerial is hard to interrupt, helps him break out of combos, and is one of the strongest of its type in the game when hit clean. His up aerial serves as an effective vertical KO option (if the situation he is in allows for it) thanks to its high knockback, and it is also safe, as his head is intangible during it and it has modest end lag.
L37: His back aerial is his fastest aerial and is debatably an even better spacing tool than his forward tilt, being fast, long-ranged, and having a cite46†sex kick -like hitbox, with a long duration and high knockback when hit clean. His air speed allows his aerial moves to be used at their fullest potential, and, except for the forward aerial, they are all decently fast.
L38: A well-known part of his playstyle is his grab game, as he has a long grab that allows for setups into the rest of his moves. Although his down throw has little to no use, every other option does to some extent. His cite47†pummel is slower compared to many others in the cast, but deals decent damage. His up throw has combo potential into his aerials, and his back throw is his primary kill throw, but his forward throw is easily his most useful one and possibly the most unique part of his character.
L39: During his forward throw, Donkey Kong can move, jump, and walk off the stage while having the opponent in his hands, acting like he usually would outside of a typical grab (aside from being unable to use his other moves and having only one jump). The move also gives Donkey Kong different types of throws based on which direction is pressed, basically giving him eight throws; these are commonly known as the "cargo throws". The cargo forward throw is often used offstage as a viable KO option.
L40: The cargo down throw is a cite48†semi-spike and works as a niche edgeguarding option. The cargo back throw does good damage and is a very solid kill throw. It also has utility as a cite49†stage spike unless his opponent can properly tech it. Finally, the cargo up throw has more combo potential than his vanilla up throw, being able to combo into his aerials at low percents. It also possesses fairly good kill power, since Donkey Kong can jump and then heave his opponents for additional height.
L41: Donkey Kong's special moves are also helpful for his gameplan. cite43†Giant Punch is his surprise KO and punish move, can be used to pressure the opponent, and has cite50†super armor if fully charged. cite17†Headbutt can cite51†bury opponents, which can allow him to setup into KOs and spikes in the air. It has super armor during the move's startup and deals very high cite52†shield damage while also having deceptively long range, giving him a shield pressure option and the ability to call out poor shield positioning.
L42: Grounded cite18†Hand Slap has a very long range and allows for stage control, but has no usage for aerial opponents, as it leaves Donkey Kong immobile and its hitbox only deals damage to grounded opponents. The aerial Hand Slap is his last move, which can meteor smash and is fast, making it effective and easy to land. His final special move, cite19†Spinning Kong , acts similarly to Bowser's cite53†Whirling Fortress as his primary cite54†out of shield option.
L43: It is hard to disrupt and is a multi-hit move with serious damage. In the air, it works as an incredibly fast horizontal recovery option and deals a lot of damage if all the hits connect. Due to the speed Spinning Kong has in the air, it can work as an effective combo breaker.
L44: However, despite his versatile moveset and high power, Donkey Kong falls into a plethora of problems. His defensive game is very poor, a common issue for characters of his size. While his massive weight gives him very high endurance, and his large frame is the reason his range is better than characters like cite35†Mario and cite55†Squirtle , it becomes a problem when having to dodge attacks, which is hard for him because he is one of the largest targets in the game.
L45: His tie hurtbox is also extremely large, further exacerbating the issue. Coincidentally, just like those two previously mentioned fighters, he has frequent trouble dealing with characters that have disjoints due to his lack of projectiles, primarily against swordfighters such as cite56†Shulk and cite57†Ike , hitboxes on moves such as cite58†Mewtwo 's up and back aerials, or fast multi-hits such as cite59†Palutena 's neutral air.
L46: Donkey Kong's size also makes him vulnerable to combos and cite60†juggling , which is worsened by his lack of combo breakers (outside of his neutral aerial and up special). The reintroduction of directional air dodges makes his aerial defense even more linear, and the new air dodge's increased ending lag hurts all characters; it debatably hurts a character such as Donkey Kong the most.
L47: Moreover, his otherwise great forward throw (cargo throw) also has certain drawbacks - notably, the risk of trying to slam the opponent into the ledge with a backward cargo throw. Due to Donkey Kong's horrid vertical recovery, if the opponent either DIs fast enough, squat jumps on him, or simply has better air reach, this attempt for an easy KO may backfire. The trajectory of both the forward and back cargo throws also possesses a minor challenge.
